Driving Through Tunnels

When driving through tunnels, it is crucial to know what to do — and especially what not to do. This is particularly important when coming to a stop in a tunnel or in the event of an accident.

💡 Lighting

Using dipped headlights is mandatory when driving through tunnels — even in illuminated tunnels. Do not rely on automatic lighting, which only activates dipped headlights once it is already dark inside. Turn on dipped headlights manually, well before entering the tunnel.

✓ Do
  • Turn on dipped headlights manually before entering
  • Keep dipped headlights on throughout the tunnel
  • Use dipped headlights even in illuminated tunnels
✕ Do Not
  • Rely on automatic lighting — it activates too late
  • Use rear fog lights inside a tunnel
  • Use full-beam headlights — these blind other drivers

🚗 Behaviour

There are few swerving options inside tunnels. Never overtake using the lane of oncoming traffic. Drive extra defensively and avoid all risks. Aggressive and antisocial driving is especially dangerous in tunnels because of the increased risk of fatal accidents.

🔧 Breakdown in a Tunnel

If you break down in a tunnel, first try to drive out of the tunnel. If you risk hindering or endangering other traffic — for example if the vehicle cannot maintain normal speed or may stop at any time — immediately turn on your hazard lights.

If leaving the tunnel is not possible, stop on the right side of the tunnel with hazard lights on. Follow these steps:

1
Stop on the right, hazard lights on

Park as far right as possible. Turn on hazard lights immediately.

2
Evacuate all passengers

Never allow passengers to sit in or stand directly next to the vehicle. Stand at least 50 metres away from the vehicle to ensure safety if oncoming traffic does not see it in time.

3
Walk to the nearest emergency telephone

Walk in the direction of traffic to the nearest emergency phone. Use it to contact the traffic controller and follow their instructions.

4
Do not use your mobile phone

Calling with your own phone is often impossible due to poor signal inside tunnels. Always use the emergency telephone.

Lay-by (emergency refuge) with phone & extinguisher
Emergency telephone
Fire extinguisher

🚨 Accident in a Tunnel

🔥
Always think of your own safety first

If there is smoke or fire, try to leave the tunnel immediately via the escape route or tunnel tube. Never turn the car around and never reverse in an attempt to exit the tunnel.

🔑
Leave the key in the ignition

This allows emergency services to move your vehicle if you have to abandon it inside the tunnel.

📞
Contact emergency services

Call 112 immediately. If there is no signal, exit the tunnel or use an emergency telephone at an emergency post.

🤝
Provide assistance

Try to warn other traffic. Help injured people if possible and necessary. If there is smoke, try to get everyone outside the tunnel.

🚶 Emergency Exit Direction Signs

These signs show the direction and distance to the nearest emergency exit. Note that walking against the direction of travel in a tunnel is always more dangerous than walking in the direction of travel — approaching traffic will see the stationary car first and are more likely to expect pedestrians on the road.

🔥 Fire in a Tunnel

The video below was produced by the Knowledge Platform for Tunnel Safety to explain what to do — and what not to do — in the event of a fire in a tunnel. The video is in Dutch but has English subtitles.

🎬 Safety Information Video

Video in Dutch with English subtitles — produced by the Knowledge Platform for Tunnel Safety.

🚫 Never do this in a tunnel fire

Never turn around or reverse inside the tunnel. Never re-enter a burning tunnel. Follow the emergency exit signs and proceed calmly on foot to the nearest exit. Stay low to avoid smoke inhalation.
